title: Plan 22: creating a product or conversion needs the whole-household MASTER_DATA_EDIT right; audit for similar gaps
body:
Raised by the victual-kit medication setup wizard ([victual-kit plan 03](https://github.com/datagen24/victual-kit/blob/main/docs/plans/03-healthkit-medication-sync.md)). Related: #696, #700, #702, #740, plan 19.

## What the wizard ran into

A household member who can consume stock cannot add a product for their own vitamin. `GenericEntityApiController::AddObject` gives shopping lists, recipes, meal plans and equipment their own permissions, and sends every other entity to `MASTER_DATA_EDIT`. `products` is not an exception. `EditObject` and `DeleteObject` use the same split. `StockApiController` also requires `MASTER_DATA_EDIT` for the barcode-lookup route that creates a product (around line 849).

`MASTER_DATA_EDIT` is one flat right. It covers products, unit conversions, locations, stores and barcodes alike. In practice it is the household administrator, so "can record that I took a tablet" and "can edit the household's master data" are separated only by handing someone everything.

This also reaches ADR-0041 mappings. A mapping to a product needs a quantity unit conversion from the mapping's unit to the product's stock unit, and the server refuses the mapping with 422 `invalid_mapping` when it is missing. The setup path for a medication therefore needs a super-user at both steps: the product and the conversion.

Read at `216af2b2` on `master`. I have not exercised each route against a running server; the conversions and stores cases follow from the same default branch, not from separate tests.

## What the client will do meanwhile

The wizard will not create master data. It maps only to what exists, names what is missing (the product, or the conversion from one unit to another), and hands off to the web UI. A key without the right gets an explanation, not a failed request. That works, but it makes every new medication an administrator task.

## To research

This looks like one instance of a broader pattern, so before choosing a fix, inventory it:

- [ ] List every write route against the permission it checks, and mark each household action that today needs `MASTER_DATA_EDIT` (or `ADMIN`) although it is not an administrative act.
- [ ] Decide for each whether the permission is right, too coarse, or missing.
- [ ] For medication specifically, choose between a narrower right (products and unit conversions only), a purpose-built endpoint that creates a stock-only product inside the consumption flow, or leaving it with administrators and documenting that.
- [ ] Check any new right against ADR-0014 (effective grants) and ADR-0018, so it cannot widen a role.

Not proposing a design here. Master data is system-wide, and changing who may write it is an authorization decision.
